class.name: TerrainBiomeLayer
class.brief_description: One climate-selected terrain material, placed by temperature and moisture.
class.description: A material the terrain paints wherever the climate falls inside this layer's Whittaker window (a temperature range crossed with a moisture range, after the biome model of the same name). Add layers to [member TerrainConfiguration.biome_layers]; at most [code]32[/code] are used. [b]How the window is evaluated.[/b] Windows are soft, not hard cutoffs. Each edge is smoothstepped over a softness of [code]max(floor, (max - min) * 0.25)[/code] (a floor of [code]0.5[/code] °C for temperature and [code]0.02[/code] for moisture), and the layer with the highest resulting weight wins. Two consequences are worth knowing: neighbouring layers blend into each other over a band proportional to their own width, and a narrow window fully contained inside a wider one can still lose to it, so a special-case layer needs a window that is genuinely distinct, not merely tighter. [b]Temperature is altitude.[/b] Temperature is derived mostly from terrain height, scaled by [member TerrainConfiguration.temperature_altitude_reference], with noise mixed in only as far as [member TerrainConfiguration.temperature_noise_influence] allows. So with default settings a temperature window selects an [i]elevation band[/i], not a region of the map: snow at the top, grass in the middle, sand at the bottom. Raise the noise influence to break those bands into patches. Moisture, by contrast, is pure noise and independent of height, it is what varies [i]within[/i] an altitude band. Temperature spans [code]-10[/code] °C to [code]30[/code] °C across the whole terrain, so windows outside that range never match. To cover the terrain fully, make sure the layers' windows overlap; a gap in the temperature axis leaves ground with no biome at all. Layers emit [signal Resource.changed], so editing one updates the terrain live.

members.member: Base colour texture for this layer. Without it the layer contributes no visible material.
Ambient occlusion map, multiplied into the layer's indirect lighting.
Human-readable label for this biome. It is what identifies the layer in the terrain dock's Whittaker chart and in the live probe readout, so it is worth filling in.

Width of the soft edge around this layer's climate box, as a fraction of the box itself. The temperature falloff spans [code]blend_softness * (max_temperature - min_temperature)[/code] either side of [member min_temperature] and [member max_temperature], and the moisture falloff the same fraction of [member min_moisture] to [member max_moisture], so a wide biome fades over a wide band and a narrow one over a narrow band without retuning. Raise it to let this biome bleed further into its neighbours, lower it for a tighter boundary. Zero gives a hard edge, down to the hair-thin falloff the shader keeps only to leave [code]smoothstep[/code]'s two edges distinct. Expect that edge to alias and crawl as the camera moves, the way any hard threshold on a smoothly varying field does. Beware that a hard edge also exposes any gap in climate coverage. A point whose temperature and moisture fall outside every layer's box gets an even blend of all of them, which the wide default falloff normally hides. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. Also applies to the CPU-side classification behind [method Terrain3D.get_biome_at], so the probed biome matches the dominant rendered one.
Height (displacement) map driving parallax occlusion mapping. Only used when [member pom_depth] is above zero.
Wettest moisture value at which this layer applies, with a soft upper edge. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

Warmest temperature, in degrees Celsius, at which this layer applies, with the same soft edge as [member min_temperature]. Since temperature tracks altitude, a high value selects [i]low[/i] ground. Range [code]-10.0[/code] to [code]30.0[/code].

Driest moisture value at which this layer applies, with a soft lower edge. Moisture is pure noise, independent of height, so this selects patches within an altitude band rather than a band of its own. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

Coldest temperature, in degrees Celsius, at which this layer applies. Below it the layer's weight smoothsteps to zero rather than cutting off. Since temperature tracks altitude, a low value here selects [i]high[/i] ground. Range [code]-10.0[/code] to [code]30.0[/code], the full span temperature can take.
Tangent-space normal map, in OpenGL convention (green channel pointing up).

Depth of the parallax occlusion effect, in UV-space units. [code]0.0[/code] disables parallax for this layer entirely, which is the cheapest option and the right one for layers with no [member height_texture]. Small values read as surface texture; large ones make silhouettes swim at grazing angles. Step counts and distance fade are shared across layers and set on [TerrainConfiguration] under [b]Parallax[/b]. Range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]0.25[/code], and it accepts larger values.
Roughness map. Read from the red channel; white is fully rough, black is mirror-smooth.

How many times the layer's textures repeat per world unit. Lower values stretch the texture over more ground; higher values tile it more tightly and show tiling artifacts sooner. Range [code]0.001[/code] to [code]2.0[/code], and it accepts larger values.
